title: Intro to OOP
summary: Object-Oriented Programming in Python: classes and instances, __init__, attributes and methods, dunder methods like __str__, and getters/setters (encapsulation), plus DRY. The step-by-step arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Write a Python class with an initializer, methods, a __str__ and a property getter/setter, and create several instances of it.

steps.title: Read the two lectures
steps.detail: Skim Intro to Python OOP and Getters & Setters. Python Crash Course ch. 9 (pp. 167–173) is the listed reading.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain class vs instance and what self means.

steps.title: Write a tiny class
steps.detail: Practice in a scratch file (not an assignment). Make a Show class with title and rating, a __str__, and a rating setter that rejects values outside 1–5. Run it with python3.
steps.doneWhen: It prints "Dark (5/5)", and Show("x", 9) raises a ValueError.

steps.title: Note the listed assignments
steps.detail: The curriculum lists Part I: Guessing Game and App Users I. Part II: the Ninja Coders demo, Student Registry, and the Crash Course reading. Stretch: OOP Budget, CSV Reader, School Interface I. Wait for Slack to confirm.
steps.doneWhen: You know which repos to expect.

concepts.meaning: A class is the blueprint; an instance is one object built from it.
The instance a method is working on.
The initializer that sets up a new instance's attributes.
A double-underscore method Python calls for you, like __str__ when printing.
Keeping data behind methods (getters/setters) so it can't be set to bad values.
Don't Repeat Yourself: put shared logic in one place.

sources: https://codeplatoon.github.io/se-curriculum/phase-I/02-OOP/1-oop-intro/assignments/ (Part I, Part II, Stretch and their repo links)
